unit.sep: Represent signed motion,calculate under explicit assumptions,observe safely and critique model scope.
unit.careers: Illustrative motion analysis,transport engineering and scientific measurement roles.
unit.focus: Terms used in linear motion; Equations of linear motion (no derivations needed),; Examples of linear motion with constant acceleration; Freely falling bodies.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional poster equates distance with displacement,negative acceleration with slowing,and a road vehicle with ideal free fall.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Path/position/velocity records,constant-a equations,piecewise motion,conditional low-drop observations and ideal frame positions.
unit.drivingQuestion: How is free fall motion important in real life? How can the dangers of free fall in our day to day life be mitigated?
unit.content: Terms used in linear motion; Equations of linear motion (no derivations needed),; Examples of linear motion with constant acceleration; Freely falling bodies.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Communication and collaboration: as the learner works with peers to discuss and present in plenary the application of linear motion in real life.
Learning to learn: as the learner carries out assignments on examples of bodies under free-fall motion and presents the findings in a group discussion.
unit.values:
Peace: the learner displays tolerance and calmness when discussing the application of linear motion in real life.
Unity: the learner displays cooperation and collaboration with others while investigating the effect of gravity on objects.
unit.pcis:
Road safety: increased awareness on how to minimise fatal injuries resulting from road crashes on sloping roads using the concept of free fall of objects.
Life Skills Education (self-awareness): the learner observes safety measures when dropping objects to investigate the effect of gravity on objects.

assessment.instructions: Independent40minutes:4readGSLM13,8Section1,12Section2,10Section3,6Section4/check/submit. Use only final reference/prompts;no keys or hints. Show units,signs and equation assumptions. Written gravity evidence is not actual-investigation certification.

sections.title: 1. Terms and signed averages
sections.prompt: For CaseA calculate distance,displacement,average speed and average velocity with direction/units. Explain why a return trip may have nonzero distance and zero displacement,and distinguish acceleration from speed.
sections.exemplar: Distance7m,displacement+3m east;average speed1m/s,average velocity+3/7≈+0.429m/s. Returning to start cancels displacement,not path length. Acceleration is velocity change per time,not speed itself;negative acceleration need not always slow an object.

sections.title: 2. Constant-acceleration variables
sections.prompt: For CaseB calculate final velocity and displacement using two consistent equations/checks. For CaseC calculate time and displacement to first rest. State sign conventions and why the equation assumptions matter.
sections.exemplar: B v2+3×4=14m/s;s2×4+½×3×16=32m;checkmean8m/s×4=32m. C t5s;s10×5−½×2×25=25m. Variables signed consistently;constant acceleration required over each interval and stopping model ends at first rest.

sections.title: 3. Gravity and investigation evidence
sections.prompt: For CaseD calculate displacement and velocity. From CaseE calculate three interval average velocities and explain the acceleration pattern without labelling them measured instantaneous endpoint speeds. State velocity and acceleration at the highest point of an ideal upward throw. Give one real recording limitation and explain whether supplied records prove an actual investigation.
sections.exemplar: D s½×10×0.60²=1.8m,v6m/s downward. E averages0.5,1.5,2.5m/s,consistent withconstant10m/s² under model;these are segment averages,not measured endpoint speeds. Atapexv0 but downwarda remainsg. Air resistance,release impulse or frame/scale error matters. Supplied records do not prove actual student drops.

sections.title: 4. Real-life significance and limits
sections.prompt: Explain why a rolling road vehicle is not ideal free fall. Give two conceptual precautions relevant to falling objects or sloping-road motion with practical limitations. Explain why a model calculation cannot certify a real safety system,and state whether any real activity or digital research occurred in this written final.
sections.exemplar: Road contact/friction/drive forces mean gravity-only freefall doesnotapply. Prevent falls/use appropriate barriers and keep people away from controlled drops;qualified road controls require real conditions and cannot be replaced by an ideal stopping number. Actual safety needs qualified design/inspection/context. Written final records show no actual activity/research.
